clue.text: A wicked exposure by 28?

parts.note: the indefinite article a has the variant form an
wicked means evil
a streak is a dash made naked in public, an act of exposure

explanation.surface: Someone wickedly flashes in public, perhaps in a novel by the author at 28.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at 28 across: this is the title of a novel by Andrea Newman, so 'by 28?' means 'a book written by her'.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrea Newman published a novel with this title, so it is a work written by that novelist.

clue.text: Elements of USA help for classic river

indicators.note: the elements, the separate letters, of the words are taken apart and put together in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Some American aid is offered for an ancient river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elements of' looks like 'some of', a hidden-word signal, but every letter of USA HELP is used, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The river god and river of Greek myth that Hercules diverted to clean the Augean stables, so a river from the classics.

clue.text: Delete English level

parts.note: to rase, an old spelling of raze, is to level a building to the ground

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove the English grade from a record.
explanation.definitionFit: To delete text is to rub it out, a synonym.

clue.text: Sung by Blake, exhibited by Fr Brown

explanation.surface: Blake's songs and Father Brown's character share a single quality.
explanation.definitionFit: Blake wrote Songs of this, and Chesterton's first Father Brown collection is The ___ of Father Brown, the priest's guileless purity.

clue.text: Double cultured novelist

parts.note: the novelist C. P. who lectured on The Two Cultures, the split between science and the arts, so his culture comes doubled

explanation.definitionFit: C. P. Snow, novelist and scientist, gave the famous Two Cultures lecture of 1959.

clue.text: Saki hero who said: "To have reached thirty is to have failed in life"

definitions.text: Saki hero who said: "To have reached thirty is to have failed in life"

parts.words: Saki hero who said: "To have reached thirty is to have failed in life"
parts.note: a quotation from the languid young dandy who gives his name to Saki's first collection of stories

explanation.definitionFit: Saki's witty young man-about-town, title character of his 1904 book of sketches, delivers that epigram.

clue.text: " not nature more than nature needs" (King Lear)

definitions.text: " not nature more than nature needs" (King Lear)

parts.words: " not nature more than nature needs" (King Lear)
parts.note: a missing word from Lear's speech to Goneril and Regan about needs, the word that opens the line

explanation.definitionFit: Lear says 'Allow not nature more than nature needs, / Man's life is cheap as beast's': the missing verb means permit.

clue.text: Friend of Carrington confuses yachters

indicators.note: to confuse is to jumble, so the letters of the clue word are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A companion of the painter muddles some sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Dora Carrington, the Bloomsbury painter, lived with the biographer Lytton Strachey.
explanation.definitionFit: Lytton, the Bloomsbury biographer, shared a house and his life with the painter Dora Carrington.

clue.text: Nobel prizewinner not content with hushed tone?

explanation.surface: A laureate is unhappy with a quiet voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a roar is a voice that refuses to stay hushed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul, American novelist, won the 1976 Nobel for literature; a roar is the very opposite of a quiet voice.

clue.text: Pangolins retrained to produce Gregorian chant

indicators.note: the scaly animals are retrained, their letters drilled into a new order

explanation.surface: Scaly anteaters are taught to sing church music.
explanation.definitionFit: Unaccompanied monophonic church music is another name for Gregorian chant.

clue.text: Forgetfulness in stale theatre production

indicators.note: in shows the answer is sitting inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A tired theatrical show is soon forgotten.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'stale' into 'theatre'; 'production' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The river of the underworld whose water made the dead forget, so its name means oblivion.

clue.text: Violinist in firm following several directions

indicators.note: following puts the firm after the compass letters

parts.note: east, north, east and south give the compass letters E, N, E, S
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A fiddler joins a company that keeps changing direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges, the Romanian violinist and composer, often went by this French spelling of his name.

clue.text: Descent of 4?

parts.note: the downfall of the novelist at 4 down, read as a weather word for flakes coming down

explanation.definitionFit: A fall of flakes from the sky is the descent of frozen precipitation, punning on the novelist's surname.

clue.text: Relaxed, yet tensed, in a way

indicators.note: in a way means after a fashion, so the letters are rearranged into another form

explanation.surface: Somebody calm, yet also somewhat tense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relaxed' and 'tensed' look like opposites in one statement, but 'tensed' is just the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedent is a rare word for seated or sitting at rest, at ease.

clue.text: Wilfred Owen's poem is rendered powerless

explanation.surface: A war poem is said to have lost its force.
explanation.definitionFit: Owen's poem about a limbless soldier carries this title; it also means made incapable.

clue.text: Verse form invented by Bentley, Evidently.

definitions.text: Verse form invented by Bentley, Evidently.

parts.words: Verse form invented by Bentley, Evidently.
parts.note: the comic four-line biographical verse that E. C. Bentley devised, named from his own middle name

explanation.definitionFit: E. C. Bentley's comic quatrain about a famous person is named after his middle name.

clue.text: Reasoned explanation to limit supply of beer

parts.note: to ration is to limit the supply of something
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A publican justifies capping the beer sold.
explanation.definitionFit: The logical basis offered for a course of action, a synonym.

clue.text: Film's ire somehow less substantial

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some new way

explanation.surface: A movie's anger seems rather thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of flimsy, which means slight or insubstantial.

clue.text: Odets's southpaw, not unlike Godot?

parts.note: the title character of Odets's Waiting for Lefty, a left-hander by nickname, who never turns up, just as Beckett's Godot never does

explanation.definitionFit: Lefty, the union man in Clifford Odets's play, is awaited throughout but never appears, like Beckett's absent figure.

clue.text: Prime audience for Scheherazade

parts.note: the chief listener to the tales of the Arabian Nights, a Muslim ruler

explanation.definitionFit: A Muslim ruler, the kind of royal listener for whom the Arabian Nights storyteller spun her tales.

clue.text: "— in mid passage his pinions from flight" (Swinburne)

definitions.text: "— in mid passage his pinions from flight" (Swinburne)

parts.words: "— in mid passage his pinions from flight" (Swinburne)
parts.note: a missing verb from a Swinburne line, meaning held back or checked

explanation.definitionFit: In the line the wings are held back, checked mid-flight, which this past tense verb expresses.

clue.text: Odd song about Lewis Carroll

indicators.note: about means scattered around, so the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A strange ditty concerns the author of Alice.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lutwidge was the real surname behind the pen name Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Operatic counter-culture

explanation.surface: An opera about the counter-culture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operatic' is short for an opera's title: Puccini's opera about poor artists in Paris. The French phrase also names the bohemian life.
explanation.definitionFit: Puccini's opera of starving artists in the Latin Quarter; the phrase also means bohemia, the unconventional artistic world.

clue.text: Some of the audiences got a surprise, others watched the clock

definitions.text: Some of the audiences got a surprise, others watched the clock

parts.words: Some of the audiences got a surprise, others watched the clock
parts.note: audiences of two symphonies by one composer, the Surprise and the Clock

explanation.definitionFit: The Austrian composer wrote the Surprise Symphony (No 94) and the Clock Symphony (No 101).

clue.text: Activated, like Macaulay's Kentish squires

explanation.surface: Country gentlemen in Macaulay's poem are stirred into action.
explanation.walkthrough: Macaulay's ballad The Armada describes beacons stirring men across England to arms, Kent's squires among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stirred into action is a synonym; Macaulay's verse has the squires of Kent woken to arms.

clue.text: Turbulent start for author of The Black Laurel!

explanation.surface: A rough beginning for a writer's career.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a turbulent outburst, a violent beginning to bad weather; Storm is also the surname of the author of that book.

clue.text: Lambeth girl in first novel

parts.note: the title heroine of Somerset Maugham's debut novel, set among the south London poor

explanation.definitionFit: Somerset Maugham's first novel (1897) is named after its Lambeth factory girl heroine.

clue.text: Edgar Allan's unknown quantity: versifying

parts.note: the American writer Edgar Allan Poe, in the possessive
y is a mathematical unknown, like x

explanation.surface: The American poet's mystery element is his verse.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for poetry or the art of writing verse.

clue.text: Flatterers like Thomas a Kempis

explanation.surface: Sycophants resemble a medieval devotional writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Imitation is said to be the sincerest form of flattery; Thomas a Kempis wrote The Imitation of Christ.
explanation.definitionFit: Copycats flatter by copying; the monk urged followers to copy Christ in his classic devotional book.

clue.text: … as well as concerning a different chap, also an author

parts.note: as well as means and
re means about or concerning
new means different, fresh
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: Continuing a sentence: this writer is about a changed man.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading dots continue from 1 across, which names a novel by this writer.
explanation.definitionFit: The British novelist and television writer behind A Bouquet of Barbed Wire.
